ai.title: Remove free-tier agent restrictions
ai.summary: Freebuff now grants all users access to code_search, list_directory, glob, code-searcher, directory-lister, and glob-matcher. Base2 agent configuration drops isFree checks, exposing these tools universally. Context pruner blacklist updated to exclude removed agent IDs. Scope limited to agents/base2/base2.ts and agents/context-pruner.ts.

eli5.text: Starting today, free-tier users can now use the assistant's built-in tools for searching code, browsing files and folders, and matching file patterns, which were previously locked behind a paid plan. If you are on the free tier, you will simply see these tools available when you open the assistant instead of them being hidden or grayed out. The assistant will also stop filtering out its own advanced helper tools in the free experience, and it cleans up old configuration that used to track who was allowed to use what.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to track a list of tasks, each item now lines up with a touch more space after its checkbox or checkmark. You'd notice the checked and unchecked items sit a bit more cleanly apart from their text. The change lands purely in how those todo lines are padded, so everything you type still behaves the same; only the alignment looks a little smoother.

ai.title: compare-cache-debug.ts adds run grouping and cachecontrol stripping
ai.summary: Updates scripts/compare-cache-debug.ts to group cache debug snapshots by runId by default, with --cross-run and --run <id> flags for filtering. Adds stripCacheControlFromMessage to ignore cache_control placement during structural diffs, reporting shared prefix length instead of binary identical/differ. This improves diagnosis of prompt cache misses by isolating conversion-layer instability from intentional cache marker shifts.

eli5.text: The tool the team uses to debug why prompt caching sometimes fails now sorts the snapshots by run by default, so it can isolate instability in the conversion layer from intentional cache-marker shifts. You can still compare across all runs with --cross-run or filter to a single run with --run <id>. When you run it, you'll see the run IDs compared and a new line showing the first message index where structural differences appear after stripping cache_control fields, instead of just saying messages differ.

ai.title: Track cache usage metrics in debug snapshots
ai.summary: Added `onCacheDebugUsageReceived` callback and `CacheDebugUsageData` type to LLM contracts. Agent runtime and SDK now emit token usage (input, output, cached) to enrich cache debug snapshots. Comparison script updated to display cache hit rates. Covers `common`, `agent-runtime`, `sdk`, and `scripts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant is configured for cache debugging, the system now records how many input, output, and cached tokens each step uses, so the snapshot file includes actual usage numbers instead of just request details. If you're collecting these debug snapshots to investigate caching, you'll now see cache hit rates and token breakdowns directly in the comparison report. This only applies to runs that pass a cache debug correlation ID, which is an opt-in behavior, so it doesn't affect standard assistant sessions.

ai.title: tmux-cli agent added to base2 default subagent set
ai.summary: New `.agents/tmux-cli.ts` defines a tmux CLI interaction agent registered as a default subagent in `agents/base2/base2.ts`. It uses structured output schema for session tracking, step results, and script issue reporting. `createBase2` now includes `tmux-cli` in the default agent list alongside `context-pruner`.

eli5.text: The base2 toolkit now ships with an automated helper that can drive a tmux terminal session from start to finish, including spinning up the session, typing commands, watching the output, and writing a brief report card on what happened. It only runs for developers who explicitly opt into the default set of base2 sub-agents, so most people won't see it until one of those scripts decides to use it. Behind the scenes, a new definition file tells the helper what to look for and how to record its findings, and a short note in the setup code tells that orchestrator to offer this helper whenever it lists the standard base2 tools.

ai.title: CLI block spacing unified via gap: 1
ai.summary: Refactored CLI message rendering to use consistent `gap: 1` spacing on flex containers instead of ad-hoc `marginTop`/`marginBottom` properties. Removed complex margin calculation logic from `ToolBlockGroup`, `AgentBranchWrapper`, and `SingleBlock`, and deleted the `block-margins` utility dependency. Updated `message-block.tsx` to apply `gap: 1` to the main column, ensuring uniform vertical spacing between text, tool, image, and agent blocks.

eli5.text: When you use the command-line assistant, the space between each line of output, whether it's text, an image, or a tool result, is now always the same. Before, different kinds of lines were spaced using separate, hard-coded margins, which sometimes made the display look uneven. The software now uses a single, built-in spacing rule on every container, and the old custom spacing logic was deleted. You'd notice that lines no longer jump or crowd each other, and the layout stays consistent as new content scrolls in.

eli5.text: This release removes paywall-style limits on core coding tools and upgrades your terminal workspace with new built-in helpers and cleaner visuals. You now get universal access to file searching, directory browsing, and pattern matching, so your AI assistant can explore code and file structures without hitting free-tier restrictions. A new terminal workspace agent is included by default, helping you manage and track work inside multi-window terminal sessions with structured reporting. The look of your to-do lists and chat messages gets a refresh too, with more even spacing and consistent layout across text, tools, images, and agent replies. A better debugging companion is added for developers, making it easier to diagnose when AI responses aren't using cached results efficiently, with new metrics showing input, output, and saved token counts.

ai.title: Opus agents pinned to amazon-bedrock provider
ai.summary: Added providerOptions.only: ['amazon-bedrock'] to all Opus-based agent definitions in agents/, including base2, editor, reviewer, thinker, and general-agent. Previously these agents used the default provider routing, causing frequent prompt cache misses when requests landed on non-Bedrock backends. Scope covers agents/base2/base2.ts, agents/editor/editor.ts, agents/editor/best-of-n/*, agents/general-agent/general-agent.ts, agents/reviewer/*, and agents/thinker/*. Opus agents now exclusively route through Amazon Bedrock, while GPT-5 and Sonnet variants remain unaffected.

eli5.text: Your coding assistant now always sends its most advanced reasoning model (Opus) to a specific, trusted provider instead of letting the system pick any available one. This provider has its own copy of the assistant's instructions, so the assistant no longer waits while those instructions are sent over again with every message, which previously caused delays and wasted time. If you use a project that relies on this advanced model, your tasks will run faster and more reliably. Other assistants you might use (like the GPT-5 or Sonnet-based ones) are not affected by this change.

The tool that draws the comparison quietly discards that stray spacing before printing the lines, so the diff you see starts and ends on actual file content. This only affects that on-screen comparison viewer in the CLI; it doesn't change the files themselves or when the comparison runs.

ai.title: Freebuff version bumped to 0.0.7
ai.summary: Version 0.0.7 is released, bundling recent base2 agent prompt fixes, Opus-to-Amazon-Bedrock provider pinning, and DiffViewer whitespace trimming. This release bump follows the 0.0.6 patch and precedes the 1.0.629 CLI increment. The version change itself is a packaging-only step; no code changes are included in this commit.
ai.evidence: Commit e119f955 modifies freebuff/cli/release/package.json, changing the version field from 0.0.6 to 0.0.7 in the freebuff package manifest. The diff is a single-line version bump with no other changes in this commit.

eli5.text: This release sharpens how Freebuff's smartest AI assistant explores your codebase and makes its top-tier AI model more reliable. The main helper agent now searches your project files directly instead of calling on older helper tools, so codebase exploration feels faster and more accurate. All of Freebuff's Opus AI agents now consistently use Amazon's Bedrock service, which means fewer mistakes and better performance when you ask complex questions. The on-screen diff viewer also cleans up extra blank lines around code changes, making it easier to read what actually changed. Together, these changes give you smarter exploration, more stable access to the best AI models, and clearer presentation of your code changes every day.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI version bumped to 1.0.629
ai.summary: Bumped the Freebuff CLI release version from 1.0.628 to 1.0.629 in cli/release/package.json. This patch-level release aggregates two days of same-day commits covering Free tier tool accessibility, Opus-to-Amazon-Bedrock provider pinning, DiffViewer whitespace trimming, CLI rendering spacing unification, and base2 agent prompt cleanup. No additional code changes ship in this version-bump commit.
ai.evidence: Commit 88818e98 modifies cli/release/package.json, incrementing the version field from 1.0.628 to 1.0.629 in a one-line diff with +1/-1 stats. No other files or code changes are present in this commit.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 1.0.629 simplifies how you start and control the coding agent, adds smarter model handling, and tidies up the terminal look and web landing page. Concrete Highlights: 1. Starting the agent is now simpler: the command-line options have been trimmed down, so you no longer pass --agent, --clear-logs, or a prompt as the first argument. You still keep the --continue and --cwd options, which let you pick up where you left off or tell the agent which folder to work in. 2. All users, including free-tier users, can now use code search, directory listing, and file pattern matching directly, instead of waiting for separate sub-agents to run. You also gain access to propose code changes and write file suggestions without restrictions. 3. The terminal output looks cleaner: todo items have better spacing, message blocks use consistent gaps, leading and trailing blank lines are removed from responses, and diffs no longer show extra empty lines at the start or end. 3. The Free tier model for minimax-m2.5 has switched to a new provider (inceptron/fp8), and all Opus-based AI models now run exclusively through Amazon Bedrock, which keeps your prompt cache faster and more reliable. 4. The landing page has been simplified with a clearer headline, 'The free coding agent', along with a new philosophy section and updated FAQs. Everyday Impact: Upgrading makes the agent quicker to launch, removes confusing command-line flags, gives every user access to powerful code-search tools, and makes the terminal output easier to read. Free-tier users benefit from broader tool access and a more responsive model, while all users enjoy a cleaner interface and faster prompt caching.

ai.title: Upgrade React to 19 across CLI and Web packages
ai.summary: React 19 replaces React 18 in CLI and Web dependencies, updating `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to 19.x. The upgrade resolves type incompatibilities with `FunctionComponent` returning `Promise<ReactNode>` in React 19. A new `react19-compat.d.ts` shim augments `FunctionComponent` to restore JSX compatibility for OpenTUI. Changes span `cli/package.json`, `web/package.json`, `freebuff/web/package.json`, and root `package.json` overrides.

eli5.text: Today, the assistant's underlying interface toolkit was upgraded to a newer major version of its base building blocks across both the command-line tool and the web dashboard. This update touched how screen readers and keyboard navigation interact with some interactive elements, so the developers added extra safety checks to keep those parts working smoothly. The changes are live now, so you don't need to do anything to receive the improvements.

ai.title: Simplify tmux-cli setup with single script execution
ai.summary: tmux-cli.ts consolidates helper script writing, session start, and command sending into a single `run_terminal_command` call via a combined bash script. base2.ts unconditionally registers 'tmux-cli' agent, removing isDefault check.

eli5.text: The assistant can run a terminal task that sets up its own workspace in one smooth step instead of doing it in several separate steps. Previously, the workspace tool only turned on for certain account types, but now it's available to you regardless of your account type, as long as it's turned on.

ai.title: Route MiniMax M2.5 through SiliconFlow
ai.summary: MiniMax M2.5 requests now route to SiliconFlow API instead of OpenRouter for free users. New `web/src/llm-api/siliconflow.ts` handles streaming and non-streaming chat completions with specific timeout configurations for deep-thinking models. Requires `SILICONFLOW_API_KEY` in environment variables. CanopyWave and Fireworks routing temporarily disabled in favor of this new provider.

eli5.text: The assistant now sends free-tier user requests to a different backend service called SiliconFlow for the MiniMax M2.5 model. If you use the free tier, your conversations route through SiliconFlow instead of the previous provider, OpenRouter. The developers turned off routing through two other services (CanopyWave and Fireworks) for now, and added a special test to check how well SiliconFlow caches repeated conversation history to save costs. You would notice this as the underlying provider change if you were watching network traffic; there is no visible change in the chat experience itself.
